results.question: How many total patients are registered in the clinic?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_patients FROM patients LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_patients FROM patients

results.question: How many doctors work in the clinic?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_doctors FROM doctors LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_doctors FROM doctors

results.question: List all unique medical specialties offered by doctors, ordered alphabetically.
results.sql: SELECT DISTINCT specialty FROM doctors ORDER BY specialty ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT specialty FROM doctors ORDER BY specialty ASC

results.question: How many total appointments were completed in 2024?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_completed_appointments FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS completed_appointments FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: What is the total invoiced revenue across all invoices?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_invoiced_revenue FROM invoices LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_invoiced_revenue FROM invoices

results.question: What is the total collected revenue from all payments?

results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_collected_revenue FROM payments

results.question: How many patients are recorded as Female?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS female_patient_count FROM patients WHERE gender = 'Female' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS female_patients FROM patients WHERE gender = 'Female'

results.question: How many appointments resulted in a no-show in 2024?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS no_show_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'no_show' AND STRFTIME('%Y', scheduled_at) = '2024' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS no_show_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'no_show' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: What is the average hourly rate of all doctors?
results.sql: SELECT AVG(hourly_rate) AS average_hourly_rate FROM doctors LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(hourly_rate), 2) AS avg_hourly_rate FROM doctors

results.question: How many invoices currently have an 'unpaid' status?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS unpaid_invoice_count FROM invoices WHERE status = 'unpaid' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS unpaid_invoices FROM invoices WHERE status = 'unpaid'

results.question: How many treatments were administered with cost greater than 100?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS treatment_count FROM treatments WHERE cost > 100 LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS expensive_treatments FROM treatments WHERE cost > 100

results.question: How many payments were made using credit cards?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS credit_card_payments_count FROM payments WHERE payment_method = 'credit_card' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS credit_card_payments FROM payments WHERE payment_method = 'credit_card'

results.question: What is the total number of appointments scheduled in the database?

results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(duration_minutes), 2) AS avg_duration FROM appointments

results.question: How many overdue invoices are there in the clinic database?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS overdue_invoice_count FROM invoices WHERE status = 'overdue' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS overdue_invoices FROM invoices WHERE status = 'overdue'

results.question: How many doctors are there in each specialty, ordered from most to least, then by specialty alphabetically?
results.sql: SELECT specialty, COUNT(*) AS doctor_count FROM doctors GROUP BY specialty ORDER BY doctor_count DESC, specialty ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT specialty, COUNT(*) AS doctor_count FROM doctors GROUP BY specialty ORDER BY doctor_count DESC, specialty ASC

results.question: What is the total collected revenue by payment method, ordered from highest to lowest?
results.sql: SELECT payment_method, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM payments GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT payment_method, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_collected FROM payments GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_collected DESC

results.question: List the top 5 doctors with the highest number of completed appointments, breaking any ties by doctor last name ascending, then first name ascending.
results.sql: SELECT d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS completed_appointments_count FROM doctors AS d JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty ORDER BY completed_appointments_count DESC, d.last_name ASC, d.first_name ASC LIMIT 5
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.first_name, d.last_name, COUNT(a.id) AS completed_count FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name ORDER BY completed_count DESC, d.last_name ASC, d.first_name ASC LIMIT 5

results.question: What is the total invoiced amount for each invoice status, ordered from highest to lowest?
results.sql: SELECT status, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM invoices GROUP BY status ORDER BY total_amount DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT status, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_invoiced FROM invoices GROUP BY status ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC

results.question: How many appointments were completed by each specialty in 2024, ordered from highest to lowest?
results.sql: SELECT d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS completed_appointments_count FROM appointments AS a JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.id WHERE a.status = 'completed' AND STRFTIME('%Y', a.scheduled_at) = '2024' GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY completed_appointments_count DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS appointment_count FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' AND a.scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND a.scheduled_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY appointment_count DESC

results.question: What is the monthly invoiced revenue for each month in 2024, ordered by month ascending?
results.sql: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y-%m', issued_at) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total_invoiced_revenue FROM invoices WHERE issued_at >= '2024-01-01' AND issued_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', issued_at) AS month, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS monthly_invoiced FROM invoices WHERE issued_at >= '2024-01-01' AND issued_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC

results.question: What is the total treatment cost per specialty, ordered from highest to lowest?
results.sql: SELECT d.specialty, SUM(t.cost) AS total_treatment_cost FROM treatments AS t JOIN appointments AS a ON t.appointment_id = a.id JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.id GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY total_treatment_cost DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.specialty, ROUND(SUM(t.cost), 2) AS total_treatment_cost FROM treatments t JOIN appointments a ON t.appointment_id = a.id JOIN doctors d ON a.doctor_id = d.id GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY total_treatment_cost DESC

results.question: Find the 5 most common appointment reasons, breaking any ties by reason alphabetically.
results.sql: SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS appointment_count FROM appointments GROUP BY reason ORDER BY appointment_count DESC, reason ASC LIMIT 5
results.gold_sql: SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS appointment_count FROM appointments GROUP BY reason ORDER BY appointment_count DESC, reason ASC LIMIT 5

results.question: How many patients were registered in each year, ordered by registration year ascending?
results.sql: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', created_at) AS registration_year, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patients GROUP BY STRFTIME('%Y', created_at) ORDER BY registration_year ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', created_at) AS registration_year, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patients GROUP BY registration_year ORDER BY registration_year ASC

results.question: List doctors hired before 2022 along with their specialty, ordered by hire date ascending.
results.sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, specialty, hire_date FROM doctors WHERE hire_date < '2022-01-01' ORDER BY hire_date ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, specialty, hire_date FROM doctors WHERE hire_date < '2022-01-01' ORDER BY hire_date ASC

results.question: What is the average treatment cost for each treatment code, ordered from highest to lowest average cost?
results.sql: SELECT treatment_code, AVG(cost) AS average_cost FROM treatments GROUP BY treatment_code ORDER BY average_cost DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT treatment_code, ROUND(AVG(cost), 2) AS avg_cost FROM treatments GROUP BY treatment_code ORDER BY avg_cost DESC

results.question: How many appointments were scheduled in the last 30 days of 2024 (from 2024-12-01 00:00:00 through 2024-12-31 23:59:59)?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS appointment_count FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-12-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS appt_count FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-12-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59'

results.question: What is the total amount paid by each payment method in 2024, ordered from highest to lowest?
results.sql: SELECT payment_method, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM payments WHERE payment_date >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND payment_date <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_amount DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT payment_method, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_amount FROM payments WHERE payment_date >= '2024-01-01' AND payment_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_amount DESC

results.question: List the top 5 patients who have the highest total invoiced amount, breaking any ties by patient last name ascending, then first name ascending.
results.sql: SELECT p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name, SUM(i.amount) AS total_invoiced FROM patients AS p JOIN invoices AS i ON p.id = i.patient_id GROUP BY p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC, p.last_name ASC, p.first_name ASC LIMIT 5
results.gold_sql: SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS total_billed FROM patients p JOIN invoices i ON p.id = i.patient_id GROUP BY p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name ORDER BY total_billed DESC, p.last_name ASC, p.first_name ASC LIMIT 5

results.question: What is the cancellation rate of appointments in 2024 as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancellation_rate_percentage FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancellation_rate_pct FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: What is the no-show rate by doctor as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, showing doctors with at least 50 total appointments, ordered by highest no-show rate descending, then total appointments descending?
results.sql: SELECT d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS total_appointments, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(a.id), 2) AS no_show_rate FROM doctors AS d JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty HAVING COUNT(a.id) >= 50 ORDER BY no_show_rate DESC, total_appointments DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.first_name, d.last_name, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(a.id), 2) AS no_show_rate_pct FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name HAVING COUNT(a.id) >= 50 ORDER BY no_show_rate_pct DESC, COUNT(a.id) DESC

results.question: Find doctors whose average appointment duration is higher than the overall clinic average duration, ordered by average duration descending.
results.sql: SELECT d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, AVG(a.duration_minutes) AS avg_duration FROM doctors AS d JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty HAVING AVG(a.duration_minutes) > (SELECT AVG(duration_minutes) FROM appointments) ORDER BY avg_duration DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.first_name, d.last_name, ROUND(AVG(a.duration_minutes), 2) AS doc_avg_duration FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name HAVING AVG(a.duration_minutes) > (SELECT AVG(duration_minutes) FROM appointments) ORDER BY doc_avg_duration DESC

results.question: What is the payment collection efficiency ratio (total payments amount divided by total invoiced amount) per specialty as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by collection rate descending?
results.sql: SELECT d.specialty, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0.0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(i.amount), 0), 2) AS collection_efficiency_percentage FROM doctors AS d JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN invoices AS i ON a.id = i.appointment_id LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON i.id = p.invoice_id GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY collection_efficiency_percentage DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH specialty_invoices AS (SELECT d.specialty, SUM(i.amount) AS total_invoiced FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN invoices i ON a.id = i.appointment_id GROUP BY d.specialty), specialty_payments AS (SELECT d.specialty, SUM(p.amount) AS total_paid FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN invoices i ON a.id = i.appointment_id JOIN payments p ON i.id = p.invoice_id GROUP BY d.specialty) SELECT si.specialty, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(sp.total_paid, 0) / si.total_invoiced, 2) AS collection_rate_pct FROM specialty_invoices si LEFT JOIN specialty_payments sp ON si.specialty = sp.specialty ORDER BY collection_rate_pct DESC

results.question: List all patients who have had appointments with at least 13 distinct doctors, ordered by count of distinct doctors descending, then patient last name ascending.
results.sql: SELECT p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT a.doctor_id) AS distinct_doctors_count FROM patients AS p JOIN appointments AS a ON p.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.doctor_id) >= 13 ORDER BY distinct_doctors_count DESC, p.last_name ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT a.doctor_id) AS distinct_doctors FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON p.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.doctor_id) >= 13 ORDER BY distinct_doctors DESC, p.last_name ASC

results.question: Find the top 3 highest-earning doctors based on total invoiced amount from their appointments, breaking any ties by doctor last name ascending, then first name ascending.
results.sql: SELECT d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, SUM(i.amount) AS total_invoiced FROM doctors AS d JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN invoices AS i ON a.id = i.appointment_id GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC, d.last_name ASC, d.first_name ASC LIMIT 3
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.first_name, d.last_name, ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS total_billed FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN invoices i ON a.id = i.appointment_id GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name ORDER BY total_billed DESC, d.last_name ASC, d.first_name ASC LIMIT 3

results.question: Which specialties have a higher cancellation rate than the clinic-wide average cancellation rate, showing their cancellation rate as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, ordered from highest to lowest?
results.sql: WITH specialty_stats AS (SELECT d.specialty, COUNT(CASE WHEN a.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS cancellation_rate FROM appointments AS a JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.id GROUP BY d.specialty), overall_stats AS (SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS clinic_avg FROM appointments) SELECT s.specialty, ROUND(s.cancellation_rate, 2) AS cancellation_rate_pct FROM specialty_stats AS s CROSS JOIN overall_stats AS o WHERE s.cancellation_rate > o.clinic_avg ORDER BY s.cancellation_rate DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH spec_rates AS (SELECT d.specialty, 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(a.id) AS cancel_rate FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id GROUP BY d.specialty) SELECT specialty, ROUND(cancel_rate, 2) AS cancel_rate_pct FROM spec_rates WHERE cancel_rate > (SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) FROM appointments) ORDER BY cancel_rate_pct DESC

results.question: For each doctor, find their rank by total completed appointments within their specialty using a window function, ordered by specialty ascending, then rank ascending.
results.sql: WITH doctor_completed_counts AS (SELECT d.id AS doctor_id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS completed_appointments_count FROM doctors AS d LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id AND a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty), ranked_doctors AS (SELECT doctor_id, first_name, last_name, specialty, completed_appointments_count, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY specialty ORDER BY completed_appointments_count DESC) AS rank_in_specialty FROM doctor_completed_counts) SELECT specialty, first_name, last_name, completed_appointments_count, rank_in_specialty FROM ranked_doctors ORDER BY specialty ASC, rank_in_specialty ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH doc_counts AS (SELECT d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS completed_count FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty) SELECT first_name, last_name, specialty, completed_count, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY specialty ORDER BY completed_count DESC) AS rank_in_specialty FROM doc_counts ORDER BY specialty ASC, rank_in_specialty ASC

results.question: List all invoices with an amount of 1100 or higher that have no corresponding payment records, ordered by amount descending, then invoice id ascending.
results.sql: SELECT i.id, i.appointment_id, i.patient_id, i.amount, i.status, i.issued_at, i.due_at FROM invoices AS i LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON i.id = p.invoice_id WHERE i.amount >= 1100.0 AND p.id IS NULL ORDER BY i.amount DESC, i.id ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT i.id, i.amount FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN payments p ON i.id = p.invoice_id WHERE p.id IS NULL AND i.amount >= 1100 ORDER BY i.amount DESC, i.id ASC

results.question: What is the average number of treatments administered per completed appointment, rounded to 2 decimals?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(t.id) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT a.id), 2) AS avg_treatments_per_completed_appointment FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON a.id = t.appointment_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH appt_treatments AS (SELECT a.id, COUNT(t.id) AS treatment_count FROM appointments a LEFT JOIN treatments t ON a.id = t.appointment_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY a.id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(treatment_count), 2) AS avg_treatments_per_appt FROM appt_treatments

results.question: Find all patients who had at least 10 appointments in 2024 and calculate their completed appointment ratio as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by total appointments descending, completion percentage descending, then patient last name ascending.
results.sql: SELECT p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name, COUNT(a.id) AS total_appointments, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(a.id), 2) AS completion_percentage FROM patients AS p JOIN appointments AS a ON p.id = a.patient_id WHERE a.scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND a.scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name HAVING COUNT(a.id) >= 10 ORDER BY total_appointments DESC, completion_percentage DESC, p.last_name ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(a.id), 2) AS completion_pct FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON p.id = a.patient_id WHERE a.scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND a.scheduled_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY p.id, p.first_name, p.last_name HAVING COUNT(a.id) >= 10 ORDER BY COUNT(a.id) DESC, completion_pct DESC, p.last_name ASC

results.question: List doctors whose hourly rate is in the top 25% of all doctors in the clinic, ordered by hourly rate descending.
results.sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, specialty, hourly_rate FROM doctors WHERE hourly_rate >= (SELECT hourly_rate FROM doctors ORDER BY hourly_rate DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT CAST(ROUND(COUNT(*) * 0.25) AS INTEGER) FROM doctors) - 1) ORDER BY hourly_rate DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH doctor_tiers AS (SELECT first_name, last_name, hourly_rate, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY hourly_rate DESC) AS quartile FROM doctors) SELECT first_name, last_name, hourly_rate FROM doctor_tiers WHERE quartile = 1 ORDER BY hourly_rate DESC

results.question: What is the monthly growth in collected payment revenue across 2024, ordered by month ascending?
results.sql: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y-%m', payment_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM payments WHERE payment_date >= '2024-01-01' AND payment_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH monthly_rev AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date) AS month, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS revenue FROM payments WHERE payment_date >= '2024-01-01' AND payment_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(revenue - LAG(revenue, 1) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS mom_difference FROM monthly_rev ORDER BY month ASC

results.question: What is the appointment drop-off rate between scheduled appointments and completed appointments in 2024 as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS completion_rate, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' OR status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS drop_off_rate FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status != 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS drop_off_rate_pct FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: How many patients dropped out after having exactly one appointment in their lifetime and never returning?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS single_visit_patients FROM (SELECT patient_id FROM appointments GROUP BY patient_id HAVING COUNT(id) = 1) AS t LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH patient_appt_counts AS (SELECT patient_id, COUNT(*) AS appt_count FROM appointments GROUP BY patient_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS single_visit_patients FROM patient_appt_counts WHERE appt_count = 1

results.question: When was the last updated appointment scheduled in 2024?
results.sql: SELECT MAX(scheduled_at) AS last_updated_appointment FROM appointments WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', scheduled_at) = '2024' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT MAX(scheduled_at) AS last_scheduled_appointment FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: What is the count of cancelled or deleted appointments in 2024?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: What is the monthly drop-off in completed appointment count from month to month in 2024, ordered by month ascending, where drop-off = previous month's completed count minus the current month's?
results.sql: WITH monthly_completed AS (SELECT SUBSTRING(scheduled_at, 1, 7) AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS completed_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' AND scheduled_at LIKE '2024%' GROUP BY SUBSTRING(scheduled_at, 1, 7)), lagged_counts AS (SELECT month_str, completed_count, LAG(completed_count, 1) OVER (ORDER BY month_str) AS prev_month_count FROM monthly_completed) SELECT month_str, completed_count, CASE WHEN prev_month_count IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE prev_month_count - completed_count END AS drop_off FROM lagged_counts ORDER BY month_str ASC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: WITH monthly_completed AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', scheduled_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS completed_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, (LAG(completed_count, 1) OVER (ORDER BY month) - completed_count) AS drop_off_count FROM monthly_completed ORDER BY month ASC

results.question: Show the drop in doctor availability: how many doctors have zero scheduled appointments?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS doctors_with_zero_appointments FROM doctors WHERE NOT id IN (SELECT DISTINCT doctor_id FROM appointments) LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS doctors_with_no_appts FROM doctors d LEFT JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.id IS NULL

results.question: What is the count of drop-ins (appointments with a scheduled duration strictly under 20 minutes)?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS drop_in_count FROM appointments WHERE duration_minutes < 20 LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS short_appointments FROM appointments WHERE duration_minutes < 20

results.question: When was the last updated invoice issued in the system?
results.sql: SELECT MAX(issued_at) AS last_issued_at FROM invoices LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT MAX(issued_at) AS latest_issued_invoice FROM invoices

results.question: What is the drop-off in payment collections: total amount of unpaid and overdue invoices combined?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_unpaid_overdue_amount FROM invoices WHERE status IN ('unpaid', 'overdue') LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS uncollected_amount FROM invoices WHERE status IN ('unpaid', 'overdue')

results.question: How many appointments were marked with a cancelled status per doctor, showing the top 10 doctors ordered by cancelled count descending, then doctor last name ascending?
results.sql: SELECT d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty, COUNT(a.id) AS cancelled_count FROM doctors AS d JOIN appointments AS a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name, d.specialty ORDER BY cancelled_count DESC, d.last_name ASC LIMIT 10
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.first_name, d.last_name, COUNT(a.id) AS cancelled_count FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY d.id, d.first_name, d.last_name ORDER BY cancelled_count DESC, d.last_name ASC LIMIT 10

results.question: Create a summary of total invoiced revenue by specialty
results.sql: SELECT d.specialty, SUM(i.amount) AS total_invoiced_revenue FROM invoices AS i JOIN appointments AS a ON i.appointment_id = a.id JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.id GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY total_invoiced_revenue DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT d.specialty, ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS total_invoiced FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN invoices i ON a.id = i.appointment_id GROUP BY d.specialty ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC

results.question: Update me on the no-show rate in 2024 as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS no_show_percentage FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS no_show_rate_pct FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01'

results.question: Clear breakdown of collected revenue by payment method, highest first
results.sql: SELECT payment_method, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM payments GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT payment_method, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_collected FROM payments GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_collected DESC

results.question: Remove cancelled appointments from the count and show completed appointments per month in 2024
results.sql: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y-%m', scheduled_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS completed_appointments_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND scheduled_at <= '2024-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month LIMIT 1000
results.gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', scheduled_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS completed_count FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' AND scheduled_at >= '2024-01-01' AND scheduled_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC
